ety.text: From Middle English varien, from Old French varier, from Latin variō (“to change, alter, make different”), from varius (“different, various”); see various.

senses.d: To change with time or a similar parameter.
ex: He varies his magic tricks so as to minimize the possibility that any given audience member will see the same trick twice.
We are to vary the customs according to the time and country where the scene of action lies.

senses.d: To institute a change in, from a current state; to modify.
ex: You should vary your diet. Eating just bread will do you harm in the end.

a. 1687, Edmund Waller, to Phyllis
Gods, that never change their state, / Vary oft their love and hate.

senses.d: Not to remain constant: to change with time or a similar parameter.
ex: His mood varies by the hour.
The sine function varies between −1 and 1.

senses.d: To display differences.
ex: The sprouting tendency of potatoes varies between cultivars, years and places of growing.

senses.d: To be or act different from the usual.
ex: I'm not comfortable with 3.Nc3 in the Caro-Kann, so I decided to vary and play exd5.

senses.d: To make of different kinds; to make different from one another; to diversify; to variegate.
ex: God hath[…] varied their inclinations.
God hath here / Varied his bounty so with new delights.

senses.d: To embellish; to change fancifully; to present under new aspects, as of form, key, measure, etc. See variation.
To disagree; to be at variance or in dissension.
ex: the rich jewel which we vary for

senses.d: alteration; change.
ex: With euery gall, and varry of their Masters,

grp.label: to change something with time or a similar parameter

Borrowed into Middle English in the 14th century from Old French variable, from Latin variare (“to change”), from varius (“different, various”). Equates to English vary + -able.

senses.d: Able to vary or be varied.
ex: variable winds or seasons; a variable quantity; a variable resistor

senses.d: Likely to vary.
ex: Lest that thy love prove likewise variable.

senses.d: Marked by diversity or difference.
Having no fixed quantitative value.
Tending to deviate from a normal or recognized type.
Something that is variable.
Something whose value may be dictated or discovered.
ex: There are several variables to consider here.

senses.d: A quantity that may assume any one of a set of values.
A symbol representing a variable.
A named memory location in which a program can store intermediate results and from which it can read them.
A variable star.
A shifting wind, or one that varies in force.
Those parts of the sea where a steady wind is not expected, especially the parts between the trade-wind belts.

grp.label: mathematics: having no fixed quantitative value
mathematics: a quantity that may assume any one of a set of values

senses.d: A deviation or difference.
A specific variation of something.
An animal or plant (or a group of such animals or plants) with characteristics causing it to differ from other animals or plants of the same species; a strain or cultivar.
ex: Jim is a nurseryman, specialising in clematis, and he has built up a business exporting 150 varieties to countries all over the world.

senses.d: A rank in a taxonomic classification below species and (if present) subspecies, and above form; hence, an organism of that rank.
ex: Capsicum annuum var. glabriusculum is a variety of Capsicum annuum commonly known as chiltepin or Indian pepper.

senses.d: A specific form of a language, neutral to whether that form is an accent, dialect, register, etc., and to its prestige level.
ex: Near-synonym: dialect (sometimes synonymous)
The mere existence of a dictionary of a certain variety of English does not automatically confer acceptance of that variety.

senses.d: A stamp, or set of stamps, which has one or more characteristics (such as colour, paper, etc.) differing from other stamps in the same issue, especially if such differences are intentionally introduced.
A collection or number of different things.
In universal algebra: an equational class; the class of all algebraic structures of a given signature, satisfying a given set of identities.
The total number of distinct states of a system; also, the logarithm to the base 2 of the total number of distinct states of a system.
The quality of being varied; diversity.
ex: Variety is the spice of life.
Age cannot vvither her, nor cuſtome ſtale / Her infinite variety: […]

From Middle French variation, from Old French variacion, from Latin variātiō, from vary + -ation.

senses.d: The act of varying; a partial change in the form, position, state, or qualities of a thing.
A related but distinct thing.
ex: When the process didn't work, we tried a variation.
All of his soups are variations on a single recipe.

senses.d: The angular difference at the vessel between the direction of true north and magnetic north.
A line of play that differs from the original.
A technique where material is repeated with alterations to the melody, harmony, rhythm, timbre, texture, counterpoint or orchestration; but with some invariant characteristic, e.g. a ground bass.
The modification of a hereditary trait.
Deviation from the mean orbit of a heavenly body.

The situation where two or more linguistic forms appear in the same environment without a change in meaning, the choice of form being determined by factors of dialect, sociolect, register or simply the speaker's preference.
An infinitesimal perturbation applied to a function, typically denoted δf, used to probe how a functional changes.
The corresponding first-order change in a functional induced by such a perturbation, typically denoted δJ[f] and called the first variation.

difference between true and magnetic (compass) north
(board games) a line of play that differs from the original
a musical technique based on an altered repetition of a theme

ety.text: From Old French variant, from Latin variāns, the present active participle of variō (“to change”). First attested in c. 1380.

senses.d: Showing variety, diverse.
Showing deviation or disagreement.
Variable.
Covariant and/or contravariant.
Something that is slightly different from a type or norm.
ex: All breeds of dog are variants of the species “Canis lupus familiaris”.

senses.d: A different sequence of a gene (locus).
A variable that can hold any of various unrelated data types.
One of a set of words or other linguistic forms that conveys the same meaning or serves the same function.
ex: The word "kerosine" is a variant of “kerosene”.

senses.d: More than one (of an indeterminate set of things).
ex: Various books have been taken.
There are various ways to fix the problem.

senses.d: Having a broad range (of different elements).
ex: The reasons are various.
The penalty for the breach of various contracts is scourging with stripes[…]

senses.d: That varies or differs from others; variant; different, sundry.
ex: a various reading of a Biblical text

ex: A small Pennsylvania university has only one varsity program: e-sports. Is this the future of college athletics?
